Agent Scraper MCP provides 6 tools with complete input schemas and reasonable descriptions. All tools are properly named with action verbs (scrape, screenshot, extract, search) and follow consistent patterns. Schemas are well-formed with proper type definitions and enums where appropriate. However, output schemas are not documented, error handling guidance is missing, and parameter descriptions lack detail about constraints and formats. The server accepts natural identifiers (URLs) and provides sensible defaults for optional parameters.

Top Issues

high Output schemas not documented. Tools return JSON strings but LLMs cannot see what fields to expect in responses. No documentation of return structure (e.g., what fields does scrape_url return besides content? What structure do links have?) response-shaper →
high Parameter descriptions lack actionable constraints. 'URL to scrape' does not explain valid URL formats, timeouts, or supported protocols. 'Dict of name → CSS selector' does not document selector syntax rules or error handling for invalid selectors. tool-description →
high No error guidance in descriptions. Tools do not document what happens when a URL is unreachable, times out, or returns an error. No recovery hints (e.g., 'If URL fails, check URL format' or 'If screenshot fails, try smaller viewport'). recovery-guide →
medium Missing result pagination guidance. tool_search_google returns 10 results by default with num_results parameter, but no documentation of maximum limits, whether results are paginated, or how to fetch additional pages beyond num_results. paginated-result →
high Output structure inconsistency. All tools return json.dumps(result), but result structure is not documented. Does scrape_url return {content, title, metadata}? Does extract_links return [{text, href}]? LLMs cannot parse unspecified structures reliably. tool →
